notes.text: Found while fixing the dsv4_tp_oproj oracle (the f64 reference multiplied the raw e4m3 byte as an integer and omitted sfa, magnitude off ~614x, which is why rel sat at exactly 1.000 -- tiny-against-large, not orthogonal). With the oracle corrected, s=1 m=1 passes at output l2 6.652e-4 and the 36 earlier outliers are gone. At s=8 the decomposed direct-cache arm shows latent rel L2 1.176e-3 with 2/65536 per-element violators, both in token 6: idx 5 got +1.166992e-1 want -1.542969e-1 (sign flip, diff 0.271) and idx 11 got -2.490234e-1 want -1.855469e-1 (diff 0.063). Three oracle accumulation models -- f64, f32 per-term, and per-128-k-block wgmma order with sfa*sfb applied once per block -- give byte-identical results, so the oracle is not the cause. Both errored elements are order 1e-1, so a rounding tail does not explain the magnitude either. Tokens 0-5 and 7 are exact, so it is not a general fp8 precision tail. Suspected device defect on a non-first m-row, first 128-n tile, m=8: candidates are the persistent 1D2D scheduler's masked/active row handling and the sfa row-to-block mapping for rows>0, neither of which m=1 exercises.

Two discriminators to run before opening the kernel investigation: sweep m over 2/4/16/32 and report which row index is wrong at each (fixed at 6 = scheduler slot or a constant in the row mapping; always second-from-last = tail masking, already weakened because m=8's bad row is 6 not 7; clean at m=16 = a path only m=8 takes), and vary the seed at m=8 (same token every seed = deterministic indexing bug; a moving row = race or uninitialized read, a different and more serious investigation).
